record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Study invariant measures for coupled map lattices and the corresponding nonequilibrium phase transitions in which those invariant measures change with the coupling.

evidence.quote: The major open problems listed in [BK2] are... the study of invariant measures for dynamical systems called Coupled Map Lattices [Ka], and of nonequilibrium “phase transitions” in which these invariant measures change as the coupling is varied.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ be a (piecewise) smooth expanding map of the interval, and for a coupling parameter $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ consider the coupled map lattice $F_\varepsilon:[0,1]^{\mathbb{Z}^d}\to[0,1]^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ defined by
$$ (F_\varepsilon x)_i \;=\; (1-\varepsilon)\, f(x_i) \;+\; \frac{\varepsilon}{|N(i)|}\sum_{j\in N(i)} f(x_j), \qquad i\in\mathbb{Z}^d, $$
where $N(i)$ denotes a fixed finite neighborhood of the site $i$ (for example, the nearest neighbors of $i$ in $\mathbb{Z}^d$). Equip $[0,1]^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ with the product topology and the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and call a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $[0,1]^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ invariant if $\mu\circ F_\varepsilon^{-1}=\mu$. Among invariant measures one distinguishes "physical" or SRB-type measures that describe the statistics of typical orbits.

Solve the following:

(a) For each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, describe the set of translation-invariant physical invariant measures of $F_\varepsilon$, and give sufficient conditions on $f$, on the geometry of $N(i)$, on the dimension $d$, and on $\varepsilon$ under which this measure is unique, mixing, and exhibits exponential decay of spatio-temporal correlations.

(b) Determine whether there exist values of the coupling $\varepsilon$ (a "nonequilibrium phase transition") at which the number, the symmetry, or the qualitative properties of the physical invariant measures change — for instance, transitions from a unique invariant measure to coexistence of multiple ergodic invariant measures, or breaking of a spatial or temporal symmetry — and characterize the critical couplings and the nature (order, universality class) of such transitions.

Provide rigorous existence/uniqueness theorems for invariant measures and rigorous proofs of the presence or absence of phase transitions for natural classes of local maps $f$ and couplings in all spatial dimensions $d\ge1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general program of describing invariant measures and nonequilibrium phase transitions for coupled map lattices remains an active research area. Partial results exist: for weak coupling, uniqueness and exponential decay of correlations have been established (Bunimovich–Sinai, Keller–Liverani, Bricmont–Kupiainen). Phase transitions have been rigorously proven in specific strongly coupled models (e.g., Gielis–MacKay; Bardet–Keller–Zweimüller relating to probabilistic cellular automata of Stavskaya type). However, a general theory characterizing all phase transitions, critical couplings, and universality classes for natural classes of expanding local maps in $d\ge 1$ is still open.

status_evidence.title: Phase Transition and Correlation Decay in Coupled Map Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of phase transitions proven via Peierls argument for strongly coupled lattices emulating Stavskaya's PCA; exponential convergence to invariant measure shown.
status_evidence.claim: Phase transitions in CMLs are rigorously established in specific strong-coupling regimes, while uniqueness/exponential decay hold for related cases.

status_evidence.title: On Phase Transitions in Coupled Map Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses construction of CMLs exhibiting phase transitions and their analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Specific examples with phase transitions are known, but a general theory is not.

status_evidence.title: Equilibrium Phase Transitions in Coupled Map Lattices: A Pedestrian Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Studies analogies with equilibrium statistical mechanics for CMLs.
status_evidence.claim: The connection to statistical mechanics is partially developed but the nonequilibrium phase transition picture is incomplete.
